build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player draws flight paths for aircraft by clicking and dragging waypoints, and planes follow the drawn paths toward their assigned runways. Score 0 if no path-drawing mechanic exists.
Proximity warnings flash when two aircraft get too close, and actual collisions result in failure with visible crash effects. Score 0 if no collision detection exists.

Aircraft enter from screen edges at different speeds with callsigns and destination indicators, requiring the player to manage multiple simultaneous routes. Score 0 if only one plane appears at a time.
Successfully landing planes on their correct runway earns points, while planes leaving the screen without landing or crashing loses lives. Score 0 if no scoring or failure system exists.
Weather events (fog, storms, crosswinds) dynamically affect gameplay by closing runways, creating no-fly zones, or altering plane behavior. Score 0 if no weather system exists.
At least 3 distinct airports with different runway configurations, surrounding terrain, and traffic patterns. Score 0 if only one airport exists.
At least 4 distinct aircraft types (small prop, commercial jet, cargo, helicopter) with different speeds and handling characteristics. Score 0 if only one aircraft type exists.
Between-level upgrades offer at least 4 options: additional runways, weather radar, speed-control commands, expanded airspace, or emergency landing pads. Score 0 if no upgrade system exists.
At least 12 levels with escalating traffic density, new aircraft types, weather complexity, and tighter timing requirements. Score 0 if difficulty never increases.
A level summary shows planes landed, near-misses, efficiency rating, and any weather events handled. Score 0 if levels end abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, control-tower themed imagery, and airport selection. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to airport/level selection to radar gameplay to level summary without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.

The radar view clearly shows aircraft positions, callsigns, drawn paths, runway assignments, and weather zones in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine aircraft state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: path drawing shows the route, proximity warnings flash and pulse, successful landings celebrate, weather changes animate in, and crashes show impact effects. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, radar view, aircraft, runways, weather effects, and menus with a consistent aviation-control palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Aircraft, runways, terminal buildings, weather icons, and terrain features use real sprite art with distinct designs readable at radar scale. Score 0 if primary elements are unstyled rectangles.

Animation brings the airspace to life: planes move smoothly along paths, weather drifts across the map, proximity warnings pulse, landing sequences animate, and radar sweeps. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with radar-screen aesthetics, aviation fonts, or control-panel styling rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
